title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right ankle just above the tip of the lateral malleolus, under a probe transverse between the malleolus and the Achilles tendon, as on ultrasound: posterior (Achilles) on the image left, anterior (peroneus brevis, fibula) on the right. Composition after NYSORA's plate (concept only), mirrored to the house laterality.
teachingPoint: The tiny sural nerve lies beside the small saphenous vein, usually just posterior to it, superficial to the deep fascia; inject around both.
claims: Right ankle between the lateral malleolus and the Achilles tendon, posterior on the left (record: behind the lateral malleolus; NYSORA probe between the malleolus and the Achilles).
Nerve beside the small saphenous vein, posterior to it (record: adjacent to the vein and usually posterior to it).
Vein and nerve in the subcutaneous tissue superficial to the deep fascia, together in one thin sheath (NYSORA; house style).
Achilles tendon posterior; peroneus brevis with the peroneus longus tendon and the fibula anterior and deep; flexor hallucis longus deep posterior with Kager's fat (standard anatomy).
Needle in-plane from the anterior end, tip beside the vein (NYSORA in-plane; same side as the superficial peroneal plate).
Teal: spread around the nerve and vein (record: inject around the nerve/vein).
Labels: Deep fascia, Sural nerve, Small saphenous vein, Achilles tendon, Peroneus brevis, Fibula.
